role: Author of native replication occurrence-slot reservation and training launch integration; bounded author verification.
conclusion: The scoped final implementation passed 13 author cases and a 112-case bounded neighborhood with the three owned production files unchanged. Full suites and remote verification are recorded by root separately.
shared_source_note: These are final read-only inventory hashes, not a claim that this author implemented or independently froze the shared request store/service.
api_and_scope: Default reserve_execution_identity(results_dir,cfg,identity,idea_id,attempt_id) and flat-owner behavior remain compatible. Descriptive replication_role/index metadata grants no exception.

An actual native launch reads replication_authorization from the trusted request-to-task mapping, current claim, confirmed source, unchanged configuration and specification. The occurrence reservation rechecks that authorization; native begin rechecks inside its owned transaction before and after creating the AttemptRef.
Native binding['replication'] survives started. The existing execution semantic SHA and B1 specification fingerprint remain unchanged; task/attempt/artifact occurrence IDs are independent.
Authorized slots are root/<identity>.replicas/<request_id>.json. They do not read, overwrite or delete the original flat owner.

The dedicated slot namespace uses the existing nonce-bound source-lock protocol with no age takeover. Canonical bounded slot metadata is written/fsynced/closed/read back; uncertain storage retains the owner/HOLD and does not authorize Popen.

Cleanup uses a captured absolute path, exact record digest and complete file stat identity. A later cfg root mutation cannot redirect cleanup; a same-content replacement inode cannot be deleted as the captured owner.

Existing slots can be replaced only for the same authorized task/request with a current confirmed native failed/not_started/requeued terminal and a new legitimate claim. Completed, open, unknown and interrupted attempts do not qualify.

No-Lake launch checks the existing database's request mapping read-only, including a newly created but not yet claimed replica. Removing the artifact contract cannot silently downgrade that task to legacy execution.
Only the precise recursive keys force_launch, replication_request_id and replication_authorization are reserved. There is no prefix-wide ban on ordinary domain configuration.

new_mechanism_acceptance.classification: New B3 mechanisms, first executed after the real request API and actual launch integration existed. Missing APIs were not tested or classified as behavioral red.

coverage: Two actual explicit requests from one confirmed native B1 source preserve exact source config and seed, execution identity and specification while creating distinct slots/attempts/artifacts; same output bytes retain the same content SHA.
Unrequested model-authored replication labels still hit ordinary completed-execution dedup.
Script, configuration and claim scope drift prevent Popen and do not reserve a slot.
A real request deletion between occurrence reservation and native begin is rejected by the second authoritative check; no native attempt or Popen is accepted.
A partial positive write followed by EIO leaves exact partial slot bytes and retained ownership; a later attempt does not blindly replace it.
Known no-Popen cleanup targets the captured slot even when cfg._orze_dir changes and another location contains a foreign slot.
RUNNING cannot be replayed. A confirmed FAILED task may use its existing authorized request after an actual bounded reset/requeue and new claim.
An unclaimed replica with no execution history still requires its native Lake; the read-only no-Lake refusal does not change database bytes or create a catalog.

defects.name: confirmed operational requeue refused
defects.mechanism: Real check_active closed a VRAM-contention attempt with outcome requeued, rotated files/claim, and restored QUEUED. Its subsequent valid claim was incorrectly refused by the draft slot terminal allowlist.
defects.repair: Permit only confirmed native requeued in addition to failed/not_started; keep interrupted unsupported.

defects.name: same-bytes inode replacement removed
defects.mechanism: During the actual GPU availability seam, another inode containing identical slot bytes replaced the captured file. Known no-Popen cleanup deleted it because the draft captured only the content digest.
defects.repair: Capture complete file stat identity during verified publication and compare it before/after read at cleanup, alongside exact digest and ownership.

final_read_only_review.note: Read the complete documentation and final owned diff. The approved boundaries match: exact request replay does not reset work; failed/not_started/requeued compatibility is retained; interrupted checkpoint resume for replica tasks remains explicit unsupported.

limitations: The request is a control-plane authorization for one fixed task, not a scientific conclusion, independent-measurement guarantee, or permission inferred from model prose.
B3 uses the existing native training process/GPU path. Tests substitute those boundaries and do not demonstrate a real CPU executor, GPU training or measured research benefit.

Filesystem slot writes and SQLite attempt commits are not atomic. An unbound/uncertain reservation can remain HOLD and may require explicit operator resolution; there is no age takeover or automatic recovery claim.
Slot files and request metadata are not security capabilities against arbitrary hostile same-user filesystem/SQL writes.
Explicit replica interrupted-checkpoint resume is not yet supported; unrelated legacy execution behavior is preserved.
Entrypoint/input drift checks do not freeze every import, interpreter package, inherited environment variable or external dataset.
No repeated-measurement aggregation, observation ranking, paid provider, holdout access, full repository suite, commit, push or remote verification is claimed in this author report.
